## Introduction

In Python, string manipulation is tightly coupled to the object (e.g. `"hello".upper()`). In R, strings are **character vectors** and manipulation is done through **functions** that act on them. This tutorial builds your base R string and regex skills from first principles — before moving to tidyverse's `stringr`, understanding the foundation makes everything click.

::: callout-note
**Learning approach:** Intuition first, syntax second. Every function is explained by *what job it does* before showing the code.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Part 1-String Fundamentals

## Creating Strings

In R, strings are called **character vectors**. Single and double quotes are interchangeable:

```{r}
x <- "Hello, Ghana!"
y <- 'Hello, Ghana!'
identical(x, y)   # TRUE — they are the same
```

A single string is a character vector of **length 1**. This is where Python users often trip up:

```{r}
length("hello")   # 1  — one ELEMENT in the vector
nchar("hello")    # 5  — five CHARACTERS in the string
```

> `length()` counts elements. `nchar()` counts characters. Always distinguish these two.

## Escaping Special Characters

Some characters need a backslash `\` to be interpreted correctly inside a string:

| Escape | Meaning              |
|--------|----------------------|
| `\n`   | newline              |
| `\t`   | tab                  |
| `\\`   | literal backslash    |
| `\"`   | literal double quote |
| `\'`   | literal single quote |

```{r}
cat("Line 1\nLine 2")       # prints on two lines
cat("Sample\tResult")       # Sample    Result
cat("He said \"positive\"") # He said "positive"
```

## `print()` vs `cat()`

These behave differently and it matters:

```{r}
x <- "malaria\npositive"

print(x)   # shows: [1] "malaria\npositive"  — R representation
cat(x)     # shows:
           # malaria
           # positive               — human-readable output
```

::: callout-tip
Use `print()` to inspect a string's R structure. Use `cat()` to see what it actually looks like as output.
:::

## Character Vectors (Strings Plural)

```{r}
fruits <- c("mango", "plantain", "pawpaw")

length(fruits)   # 3  — three elements
nchar(fruits)    # 5 8 6 — character count of EACH element
```

Most base R string functions are **vectorized** — they work on every element automatically, with no loop needed. This is a powerful R idiom.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Part 2 — Core Base R String Functions

## Group 1: Building & Combining — `paste()` and `paste0()`

`paste()` joins strings together. The `sep` argument controls what goes *between arguments*:

```{r}
paste("malaria", "diagnostics")             # "malaria diagnostics"
paste("malaria", "diagnostics", sep = "-")  # "malaria-diagnostics"
paste0("sample", 3)                         # "sample3"  (sep = "" by default)
```

The `collapse` argument squishes a **vector** into a single string:

```{r}
labs <- c("haematology", "microbiology", "parasitology")

paste(labs, sep = "-")      # does nothing useful here
# "haematology" "microbiology" "parasitology"  — still 3 elements

paste(labs, collapse = "-") # collapses into ONE string
# "haematology-microbiology-parasitology"
```

::: callout-important
**`sep` vs `collapse`:**

- `sep` → what goes between *arguments* (e.g. `paste("a", "b", sep="-")`)
- `collapse` → what goes between *vector elements* when squishing many into one
:::

## Group 2: Measuring & Extracting — `nchar()` and `substr()`

```{r}
x <- "Plasmodium falciparum"

nchar(x)          # 21
substr(x, 1, 10)  # "Plasmodium"   (start, stop — 1-indexed!)
substr(x, 12, 21) # "falciparum"
```

`substr()` also does **in-place replacement**:

```{r}
x <- "malaria case"
substr(x, 1, 7) <- "MALARIA"
x   # "MALARIA case"
```

Vectorized over a vector of strings:

```{r}
samples <- c("PF001", "PF002", "PF003")
substr(samples, 3, 5)   # "001" "002" "003"
```

## Group 3: Case & Whitespace — `toupper()`, `tolower()`, `trimws()`

```{r}
toupper("pfhrp2")   # "PFHRP2"
tolower("HRP2")     # "hrp2"
```

`trimws()` removes leading/trailing whitespace — essential when reading messy lab data:

```{r}
trimws("  positive  ")                    # "positive"
trimws("  positive  ", which = "left")    # "positive  "
trimws("  positive  ", which = "right")   # "  positive"
```

::: callout-tip
When importing lab result data, someone often types `" Positive"` with a stray space. `trimws()` + `tolower()` together normalizes these reliably.
:::

## Group 4: Splitting — `strsplit()`

Splits a string on a delimiter. Returns a **list** (because different elements may split into different numbers of pieces):

```{r}
x <- "pfhrp2;pfhrp3;kelch13"
strsplit(x, ";")
# [[1]]
# [1] "pfhrp2"  "pfhrp3"  "kelch13"
```

Use `[[1]]` to extract the vector from the list:

```{r}
genes <- strsplit(x, ";")[[1]]
genes[2]   # "pfhrp3"
```

Vectorized over multiple strings:

```{r}
samples <- c("PF-001-pos", "PF-002-neg")
strsplit(samples, "-")
# [[1]]  "PF" "001" "pos"
# [[2]]  "PF" "002" "neg"
```

## Group 5: Searching — `grep()` and `grepl()`

These are your **"find which strings match"** tools:

| Function  | Returns                         | Think of it as      |
|-----------|---------------------------------|---------------------|
| `grepl()` | logical vector (`TRUE`/`FALSE`) | "does it match?"    |
| `grep()`  | integer indices (or values)     | "which ones match?" |

```{r}
results <- c("positive", "negative", "positive", "invalid", "negative")

grepl("pos", results)              # TRUE FALSE TRUE FALSE FALSE
grep("pos", results)               # 1 3
grep("pos", results, value = TRUE) # "positive" "positive"
```

Use `grepl()` for filtering with `[]`:

```{r}
results[grepl("pos", results)]   # "positive" "positive"
```

::: callout-note
**Memory aid:** `grepl` = **grep logical** — same as `grep` but returns `TRUE`/`FALSE` instead of positions.
:::

## Group 6: Replacing — `sub()` and `gsub()`

| Function | Replaces                     |
|----------|------------------------------|
| `sub()`  | **first** match only         |
| `gsub()` | **all** matches (g = global) |

```{r}
x <- "the patient tested positive, positive"

sub("positive", "POSITIVE", x)    # "the patient tested POSITIVE, positive"
gsub("positive", "POSITIVE", x)   # "the patient tested POSITIVE, POSITIVE"
```

Vectorized — works element-by-element on a vector:

```{r}
ids <- c("sample_001", "sample_002", "sample_003")
gsub("sample_", "PF", ids)   # "PF001" "PF002" "PF003"
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Part 3 — Regular Expressions in R

## The Core Idea

A regular expression (regex) is a **pattern language** — it describes the *shape* of text, not just exact characters.

Instead of asking *"does this equal 'positive'?"* you ask *"does this contain a word starting with 'p' and ending in 'e'?"*

In R, regex patterns slot into the functions you already know:

```{r}
grepl("pattern", x)    # x is your string or vector
gsub("pattern", "replacement", x)
```

## Literal Characters

The simplest regex is exact text:

```{r}
grepl("malaria", c("malaria positive", "typhoid", "malaria negative"))
# TRUE FALSE TRUE
```

## The Dot `.` — Any Character

`.` matches **any single character** (except newline):

```{r}
grepl("P.003", c("PF003", "PX003", "P003", "PFF003"))
# TRUE   TRUE   FALSE    FALSE
```

To match a **literal dot**, escape it with `\\.`:

```{r}
grepl("3\\.14", c("3.14", "3X14"))   # TRUE FALSE
```

::: callout-important
**R double-backslash rule:** R's string parser reads `\` first. So to pass `\.` to the regex engine, you must write `\\.` in R — the first `\` escapes the second for R, delivering `\.` to regex.
:::

## Character Classes `[ ]`

Square brackets define a **set of allowed characters** at one position:

```{r}
grepl("P[FX]003", c("PF003", "PX003", "PZ003"))
# TRUE   TRUE    FALSE
```

Ranges:

```{r}
# [a-z]       any lowercase letter
# [A-Z]       any uppercase letter
# [0-9]       any digit
# [a-zA-Z]    any letter
# [a-zA-Z0-9] any alphanumeric
```

Negation with `^` **inside** brackets:

```{r}
grepl("[^0-9]", c("PF001", "12345"))
# TRUE  FALSE
# "PF001" contains non-digit characters; "12345" does not
```

## Shorthand Character Classes

| Shorthand | Meaning            | Equivalent              |
|-----------|--------------------|-------------------------|
| `\\d`     | any digit          | `[0-9]`                 |
| `\\D`     | any non-digit      | `[^0-9]`                |
| `\\w`     | word character     | `[a-zA-Z0-9_]`          |
| `\\W`     | non-word character | `[^a-zA-Z0-9_]`         |
| `\\s`     | whitespace         | space, tab, newline     |
| `\\S`     | non-whitespace     | anything but whitespace |

```{r}
grepl("\\d", c("PF001", "falciparum"))         # TRUE  FALSE
grepl("\\s", c("P falciparum", "Pfalciparum")) # TRUE  FALSE
grepl("\\w+", c("pfhrp2", "---"))              # TRUE  FALSE
```

## Anchors `^` and `$`

Anchors match **positions**, not characters:

| Anchor | Matches         |
|--------|-----------------|
| `^`    | start of string |
| `$`    | end of string   |

```{r}
x <- c("positive", "false positive", "positive result")

grepl("positive", x)     # TRUE TRUE TRUE  — anywhere in string
grepl("^positive", x)    # TRUE FALSE TRUE — must START with it
grepl("positive$", x)    # TRUE TRUE FALSE — must END with it
grepl("^positive$", x)   # TRUE FALSE FALSE — must be EXACTLY this
```

::: callout-tip
`^` and `$` together are your **validation anchors** — use them to enforce that an entry matches a format exactly, not just contains a substring.
:::

## Quantifiers — How Many Times?

Quantifiers attach to the character or class *immediately before* them:

| Quantifier | Meaning           |
|------------|-------------------|
| `?`        | 0 or 1 (optional) |
| `*`        | 0 or more         |
| `+`        | 1 or more         |
| `{n}`      | exactly n         |
| `{n,}`     | at least n        |
| `{n,m}`    | between n and m   |

```{r}
x <- c("colour", "color", "colouur")

grepl("colou?r", x)      # TRUE TRUE FALSE  — u is optional (0 or 1)
grepl("colou{1}r", x)    # TRUE FALSE FALSE — exactly one u
grepl("colou{1,2}r", x)  # TRUE FALSE TRUE  — one or two u's
```

Practical sample ID validation:

```{r}
ids <- c("PF1", "PF12", "PF123", "PF1234")
grepl("^PF\\d{3}$", ids)   # FALSE FALSE TRUE FALSE — exactly 3 digits
```

## Alternation `|` — OR Logic

```{r}
grepl("positive|negative", c("positive", "negative", "invalid", "pos"))
# TRUE TRUE FALSE FALSE
```

Group with parentheses to scope the OR:

```{r}
grepl("^(positive|negative)$", c("positive", "negative", "false positive"))
# TRUE  TRUE  FALSE
```

## Capture Groups `( )` and Backreferences

Parentheses serve two purposes:

**1. Grouping** — scope quantifiers and alternation:

```{r}
grepl("(ha)+", c("ha", "haha", "hahaha", "h"))
# TRUE TRUE TRUE FALSE — "ha" repeated one or more times
```

**2. Capture groups** — remember what was matched, reuse in `gsub()`:

`\\1` refers to what group 1 captured, `\\2` to group 2, etc.

```{r}
x <- c("falciparum_PF001", "vivax_PV002")

gsub("(\\w+)_(\\w+)", "\\2-\\1", x)
# "PF001-falciparum"  "PV002-vivax"
# group 1 = species name, group 2 = sample ID — swapped with \\2-\\1
```

## Practical Examples

**1. Validate sample IDs** — must be 2 uppercase letters + 3 digits:

```{r}
ids <- c("PF001", "pf001", "PF01", "PF0012", "XX999")
grepl("^[A-Z]{2}\\d{3}$", ids)
# TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE
```

**2. Find gene names in lab notes:**

```{r}
notes <- c("deletion of pfhrp2 confirmed", "pfhrp3 intact", "no deletion found")
grepl("pfhrp[23]", notes)
# TRUE  TRUE  FALSE

grep("pfhrp[23]", notes, value = TRUE)
# "deletion of pfhrp2 confirmed"  "pfhrp3 intact"
```

**3. Normalize messy lab result entries:**

```{r}
results <- c("  Positive ", "NEGATIVE", "pos.", "Neg")

results <- tolower(trimws(results))  # lowercase + strip whitespace
results <- gsub("[^a-z]", "", results)  # remove non-letter characters
results
# "positive" "negative" "pos" "neg"
```

**4. Reformat IDs by inserting a separator:**

```{r}
ids <- c("PF001", "PF002", "PF003")
gsub("(PF)(\\d+)", "\\1-\\2", ids)
# "PF-001"  "PF-002"  "PF-003"
```

## Part 4 — Summary Cheat Sheet

## Base R String Functions

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: false
# Reference table — see rendered cheat sheet below
```

::: panel-tabset
### String Functions

| Function | Purpose | Key Arguments | Example |
|-----------------|-----------------|-----------------------|-----------------|
| `nchar(x)` | Count characters | — | `nchar("pfhrp2")` → `6` |
| `paste(...)` | Combine strings | `sep`, `collapse` | `paste("a","b",sep="-")` → `"a-b"` |
| `paste0(...)` | Combine (no space) | `collapse` | `paste0("PF",1)` → `"PF1"` |
| `substr(x, start, stop)` | Extract substring | `start`, `stop` | `substr("PF001",3,5)` → `"001"` |
| `toupper(x)` | Convert to uppercase | — | `toupper("pfhrp2")` → `"PFHRP2"` |
| `tolower(x)` | Convert to lowercase | — | `tolower("HRP2")` → `"hrp2"` |
| `trimws(x)` | Remove whitespace | `which` (`"both"`, `"left"`, `"right"`) | `trimws(" pos ")` → `"pos"` |
| `strsplit(x, split)` | Split into pieces | `split` (can be regex) | `strsplit("a;b",";")[[1]]` → `c("a","b")` |
| `grepl(pattern, x)` | Logical match test | `ignore.case` | `grepl("pos","positive")` → `TRUE` |
| `grep(pattern, x)` | Indices of matches | `value`, `ignore.case` | `grep("pos", x)` → positions |
| `sub(pattern, repl, x)` | Replace first match | `ignore.case` | `sub("a","A","banana")` → `"bAnana"` |
| `gsub(pattern, repl, x)` | Replace all matches | `ignore.case` | `gsub("a","A","banana")` → `"bAnAnA"` |
| `sprintf(fmt, ...)` | Format strings | `fmt` | `sprintf("%.2f", 3.1)` → `"3.10"` |
| `startsWith(x, prefix)` | Test string start | `prefix` | `startsWith("PF001","PF")` → `TRUE` |
| `endsWith(x, suffix)` | Test string end | `suffix` | `endsWith("PF001","01")` → `TRUE` |
| `chartr(old, new, x)` | Replace characters | `old`, `new` | `chartr("aeiou","AEIOU","hello")` |
| `format(x)` | Format for display | `width`, `justify` | `format(3.1,nsmall=2)` → `"3.10"` |

### Regex Syntax

| Pattern  | Meaning                       | Example Match                      |
|----------|-------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `abc`    | Literal characters            | `"abc"` in `"abcdef"`              |
| `.`      | Any single character          | `"P.003"` matches `"PF003"`        |
| `\\.`    | Literal dot                   | `"3\\.14"` matches `"3.14"` only   |
| `[abc]`  | Any of a, b, c                | `"[PX]F"` matches `"PF"` or `"XF"` |
| `[^abc]` | Anything except a, b, c       | `"[^0-9]"` matches non-digits      |
| `[a-z]`  | Range: any lowercase letter   | —                                  |
| `[A-Z]`  | Range: any uppercase letter   | —                                  |
| `[0-9]`  | Range: any digit              | —                                  |
| `\\d`    | Any digit                     | `"\\d+"` matches `"123"`           |
| `\\D`    | Any non-digit                 | —                                  |
| `\\w`    | Word character `[a-zA-Z0-9_]` | —                                  |
| `\\W`    | Non-word character            | —                                  |
| `\\s`    | Whitespace                    | `"\\s+"` matches spaces/tabs       |
| `\\S`    | Non-whitespace                | —                                  |
| `^`      | Start of string               | `"^PF"` — must start with PF       |
| `$`      | End of string                 | `"\\d$"` — must end with digit     |
| `?`      | 0 or 1 (optional)             | `"colou?r"` → color or colour      |
| `*`      | 0 or more                     | `"ab*"` → a, ab, abb, ...          |
| `+`      | 1 or more                     | `"ab+"` → ab, abb, ...             |
| `{n}`    | Exactly n                     | `"\\d{3}"` → exactly 3 digits      |
| `{n,m}`  | Between n and m               | `"\\d{2,4}"` → 2 to 4 digits       |
| `a\|b`   | a OR b                        | `"pos\|neg"` matches either        |
| `(abc)`  | Capture group                 | `"(\\w+)_(\\w+)"`                  |
| `\\1`    | Backreference to group 1      | Used in `gsub()` replacement       |

### Common Patterns

| Task | Pattern | Code |
|---------------------|-------------------------------|---------------------|
| Exact match only | `^pattern$` | `grepl("^positive$", x)` |
| Starts with | `^prefix` | `grepl("^PF", x)` |
| Ends with | `suffix$` | `grepl("001$", x)` |
| Contains digits | `\\d` | `grepl("\\d", x)` |
| Only digits | `^\\d+$` | `grepl("^\\d+$", x)` |
| Only letters | `^[a-zA-Z]+$` | `grepl("^[a-zA-Z]+$", x)` |
| Sample ID format (2 letters + 3 digits) | `^[A-Z]{2}\\d{3}$` | `grepl("^[A-Z]{2}\\d{3}$", x)` |
| Remove whitespace | `\\s+` | `gsub("\\s+", "", x)` |
| Remove non-alphanumeric | `[^a-zA-Z0-9]` | `gsub("[^a-zA-Z0-9]", "", x)` |
| One of several values | `^(val1\|val2)$` | `grepl("^(pos\|neg)$", x)` |
| IP-like pattern | `\\d+\\.\\d+` | `grepl("\\d+\\.\\d+", x)` |
| Empty string | `^$` | `grepl("^$", x)` |
| Non-empty string | `.+` | `grepl(".+", x)` |

### Key Distinctions

| Comparison | Details |
|---------------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| `length()` vs `nchar()` | `length()` counts vector elements; `nchar()` counts characters within each string |
| `print()` vs `cat()` | `print()` shows R representation (with quotes); `cat()` renders actual output |
| `sep` vs `collapse` in `paste()` | `sep` between arguments; `collapse` squishes a vector into one string |
| `sub()` vs `gsub()` | `sub()` replaces first match; `gsub()` replaces all matches |
| `grep()` vs `grepl()` | `grep()` returns positions/values; `grepl()` returns TRUE/FALSE |
| `^` inside `[ ]` vs outside | Inside `[^abc]` = negation; outside `^abc` = start of string anchor |
| `\\.` vs `.` | `\\.` = literal dot; `.` = any character |
| `\\1` in replacement | Backreference to capture group 1 — use in `gsub()` replacement string |
:::
